methods.label: Factor and bound positive factors
methods.explanation:
First factor the given quadratic to find the allowed values of \(x\):
\[
(x-2)(x-3)<0.
\]
The product is negative exactly when the two factors have opposite signs, which occurs for \(2<x<3\). At either endpoint the product is zero, so neither endpoint is allowed.

Now factor the expression we want to bound:
\[
P=(x+2)(x+3).
\]
From \(2<x<3\), we have \(4<x+2<5\) and \(5<x+3<6\). All these quantities are positive, so multiplying their bounds gives
\[
20=4\cdot5<(x+2)(x+3)<5\cdot6=30.
\]
Thus \(20<P<30\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
